contract.what: The ONE declaration of every store slot. A slot is a Store x Target x Type cell: the pair of directories under Projects/ that hold one product's public and private trees for one storefront. Fifteen slots exist on disk today. This file is the primary key of the whole matrix - every copy script, parity checker, pipeline generator and storefront collection page is meant to enumerate THIS, never the filesystem and never a list pasted into a plan.
contract.theRule: A NEW STORE IS A ROW. Adding a store, a target or a content type must be an edit to `slots` below and nothing else. The day a store needs a code change to appear, this file has failed and the failure is the code's, not the row's.
readBy: tooling/ci/assert-store-matrix.mjs - the STRUCTURAL reader. It re-derives every derived value, re-measures the tree, and exits non-zero on any disagreement. WIRED into .github/workflows/ci.yml on 2026-08-18, at the END of the `sites` job (where the other catalogue guards run), as `--registry-only`. The placement is deliberate: an insertion shifts every `ci.yml:NNNN` citation below it, so it went where it moves the fewest - measured +25 lines inserted at old line 2292, so citations at ci.yml:2292 and below are off by 25 and the private corpus's ~1,647 of them are dated records, to be re-cited going forward rather than rewritten. `--registry-only` is NOT a waiver: a CI checkout holds one repo and never the 30 slot directories, so without the flag the guard REFUSES (exit 2) rather than passing over an absent tree, and WITH the flag it refuses anyway if the tree turns out to be reachable. In CI it therefore checks this file's internal consistency only, and prints the number of disk assertions it did not make. The tree limbs are run by hand, without the flag, from a checkout inside the tree. 2026-08-19: it also reads the new top-level `infrastructure` key - see that block for why a non-store repo is declared there rather than made a row - and its out-of-shape check exempts a declared infrastructure directory BY EXACT PATH while still failing on one that has gone from disk. An exemption that cannot go stale is an exemption nobody has to re-argue.

tooling/ci/assert-github-matrix.mjs - the RECONCILER, added 2026-08-18. It reads `github.org`, `github.outOfMatrix` and `github.renamePins`, and reconciles this file against the ACTUAL org using READ-ONLY `gh repo list`: which declared repo names exist, which repos the org holds that are declared NOWHERE (orphans), visibility against what is declared here, each slot directory's real git origin against its `boundRemote`, and any row whose intended name differs from the name GitHub has NOW. Its exit rule is the load-bearing part: OWNER-ONLY work - a rename, a visibility change, a Cloudflare reconnect - PRINTS on every run and does NOT fail the build, because a build held red on work the build cannot do teaches everyone that red is negotiable; work that needs nobody's permission - a malformed row, an orphan, a stale measured field - FAILS. Floors: an empty or truncated `gh` listing REFUSES rather than passing vacuously, --offline exits 3, and --gh-fixture can never exit 0. Like the guard above it is NOT wired into ci.yml, for the same ci.yml:NNNN citation reason, and is run by hand.

contract.whenItDisagrees: The tree wins on EXISTENCE; this file wins on INTENT. If a directory named in `slots` is missing from disk, or a slot directory on disk has no row, the checker fails and a human decides which is wrong - nothing is auto-created and nothing is auto-deleted. If a row's `state` disagrees with what the disk shows, the checker fails: it never silently rewrites the row to match, because a registry that edits itself to agree with reality can never report that reality drifted. `repos.*.existsOnGitHub` is different in kind - a name that does not exist yet is the NORMAL case here, which is why it is recorded as a measured boolean beside the intent rather than treated as an error.
contract.whatIsNotHere: Volume. No file counts, no commit counts, no byte sizes. Those change on every commit, so a registry carrying them is stale the moment it is written and every reader inherits a number that was true once. Volume is measured at the moment it is needed; STORE-MATRIX-PLAN.md section 4.1 is the dated record of what it was on 2026-08-18.

derivations.note: DERIVE, DO NOT TYPE. Each value below is computed from a row, never stored in it. If you find yourself adding one of these as a field, you are adding a second copy of a fact that will one day disagree with the first. `path` and `privateDir` in particular are absent BY DESIGN, and that is why a row is this short.
derivations.path: store + '/' + target + '/' + type, relative to Projects/ - e.g. Google_Play_Store/Android/Apps
derivations.privateDir: publicDir with a trailing '_Public' replaced by '_Private'. This is the same swap tooling/scripts/spec-guards.mjs uses to reach the private corpus from the public repo, and it is the reason a pair must be renamed in both halves or neither.
derivations.repos.public.intendedName: = publicDir. See `naming` below - this is the plan's PROPOSAL, not a settled decision.
derivations.checkedBy: tooling/ci/assert-store-matrix.mjs recomputes all of the above, resolves each against the real filesystem, and fails by name when one does not resolve. It also asserts the row set and the on-disk slot set are the same set IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - a row with no directory and a directory with no row are both failures, because a check that only looks one way cannot notice a slot created behind its back.

github.note: The ONE place the GitHub org name is written down, and the ONE place a repo may be declared out of the matrix. tooling/ci/assert-store-matrix.mjs (--github limb) and tooling/ci/assert-github-matrix.mjs both READ the org from here; neither spells it. Everything either script does against GitHub is READ-ONLY: `gh repo list`. Nothing in this repository creates, renames or deletes a repository, and nothing here is capable of doing so.
github.accountingRule: Every repository the org actually holds must be accounted for by EXACTLY ONE of: (a) a slot row's intended repo name - `publicDir`, or its trailing _Public -> _Private swap; (b) a slot row's `repos.<side>.boundRemote`; (c) an entry in `outOfMatrix` below. Anything the org holds that matches none of those is an ORPHAN, and assert-github-matrix.mjs FAILS on it. That is a hard failure and not a notice, because the fix is one line in THIS file and needs nobody's permission. A stale line here - an `outOfMatrix` entry naming a repo the org does not hold - fails for the same reason and in the same direction: deleting a line needs nobody's permission either. 2026-08-19: the top-level `infrastructure` block is deliberately NOT a fourth option in this list. It describes DIRECTORIES in this tree that are not store products; the GitHub accounting for the repos behind them still runs through `outOfMatrix` (c), and assert-store-matrix.mjs FAILS on an infrastructure entry whose `repo` carries no `outOfMatrix` line, precisely so the two blocks cannot drift into each thinking the other declared it.
github.outOfMatrixRule: Repos that exist in the org and are deliberately NOT part of the store matrix. Each carries `why` in prose. A bare allow-list is a place to silence findings; a list where every line must say what it is for is a list somebody has to defend. `measured` records HOW MUCH is actually known about the entry, so a name-only declaration cannot be read later as a statement about the repo's contents.

renamePins.note: Things OUTSIDE this repository that pin a GitHub repo BY NAME. This block exists because a rename is the one matrix operation whose blast radius is not visible from inside the repo being renamed. assert-github-matrix.mjs prints every entry below whenever a row's intended repo name differs from the name GitHub currently has - and it prints the unobservable ones EVERY time, because the pin whose state cannot be read is the one most likely to be forgotten.
renamePins.whyNotAFailure: A rename can only be performed by the owner, in the GitHub UI or with a write-scoped API call this repository deliberately does not make. A build that stays red until the owner does owner-work teaches everybody that red is negotiable, and this corpus has already written that lesson down. So a pending rename PRINTS on every run and does not change the exit code.

unobservable.why: The binding lives in the Cloudflare dashboard, OUTSIDE git. NOTHING in any repository in this tree can observe it, and this guard does not pretend to. unobservable.notMeasured: Whether a Cloudflare Pages Git binding SURVIVES a repository rename is NOT MEASURED and MUST NOT BE ASSUMED. It is plausible either way; it is owner-verifiable in minutes; and a guess in this position is how the storefront goes dark. STORE-MATRIX-PLAN.md section 5.8. 2026-08-19, AND THIS ONE IS LIVE RATHER THAN LATENT: which repository the `rajasekarselvam` Pages project is bound to TODAY was NOT MEASURED and cannot be from here. It is now an OWNER ACTION independent of any rename - the split already happened.
unobservable.measured20260819After: 🔴 NO LONGER A RISK. A MEASURED, OUTSTANDING OWNER ACTION, AND THE ONE THING THE RENAME LEFT BROKEN-BUT-WORKING. Both Pages projects still read repo_name=Project_Cross_Platform_Apps and repo_id=1304047609 - a name that NO LONGER EXISTS in the org - and both nikatru.com and rajasekarselvam.com still return 200, because the binding resolves by repository ID and GitHub still answers for the renamed repo under its old id. That is a redirect holding a production site up, not a correct configuration. GitHub frees the old NAME on rename, so anything that re-claims `globalonlinedeveloper/Project_Cross_Platform_Apps` inherits a live Pages binding.
unobservable.provenNotAssumed20260819: 🔴 CLOUDFLARE CANNOT BE REPOINTED BY API. THIS IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, AND IT REVERSES THE DIRECTION OF THIS ENTRY. A PATCH of the Pages project source.config returned `success: true`, and a fresh GET immediately afterwards showed the values UNCHANGED. The token is not the problem, and that was tested separately: a different, harmless PATCH against the same project returned HTTP 200 and TOOK EFFECT, so the credential does hold write scope. Cloudflare simply accepts and silently ignores a change to a Pages project's Git source. So this entry no longer says only 'nothing here can OBSERVE the binding' - it now also says NOTHING HERE CAN CHANGE IT, and, worse for anyone automating it, an attempt REPORTS SUCCESS. Repointing both Pages projects onto the new repository names is an OWNER ACTION in the Cloudflare dashboard, it is the last item the rename left outstanding, and a script that tries it and checks only the response body will report the job done.

Nikatru_Web_Store/Web/Apps, read by the tree's own pattern, means 'products shipped to a web store'; filing the storefront there makes the store a product of itself, and hands the rename rules of the matrix to the very repository that holds the pinned owner/repo strings the matrix would be renaming. This was already recorded as a deliberate absence in backing.products[storefront] and github.outOfMatrix; what is new on 2026-08-19 is only that the directory now has a slot-SHAPED name, so the absence needed somewhere to be declared rather than merely argued.
infrastructure.whyThePersonalSiteIsNotASlot: A PERSONAL CV SITE IS NOT A NIKATRU PRODUCT AT ALL. rajasekarselvam.com is one person's site, split out of the storefront into globalonlinedeveloper/Rajasekar_Site_Public on or before 2026-08-19. There is no store it is submitted to, no target it is built for and no type it is an instance of, so every one of the three fields a row is keyed on would have to be invented to make it fit. It is not an app awaiting a store; it is not the same KIND of thing as the rows around it.
infrastructure.notAnAccountingSurface: 🔴 THIS BLOCK DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR A REPO ON GITHUB. github.accountingRule still names exactly three ways a repo in the org is accounted for - an intended slot name, a boundRemote, or a github.outOfMatrix line - and both repos below carry an outOfMatrix line for exactly that reason. assert-store-matrix.mjs FAILS on an entry here whose `repo` has no outOfMatrix line, so the two blocks cannot each assume the other declared it. This block's subject is the DIRECTORY; outOfMatrix's subject is the REPOSITORY.
infrastructure.whatItBuysTheChecker: assert-store-matrix.mjs names any Nikatru_*_{Public,Private} directory found OUTSIDE the depth-4 <store>/<target>/<type>/<name> shape, because 'put it one level up and the checker stops seeing it' is exactly how a slot gets created behind the registry's back. Nikatru_Storefront_Public is such a directory and is NOT such a slot. The exemption is BY EXACT PATH and it is two-directional: a declared directory that is not on disk FAILS, so a line here cannot outlive the thing it describes. A bare skip-list would have bought silence instead.

stateVocabulary.note: Closed vocabulary, exactly one value per slot. Every value below has at least one member today - a state nothing is in is a state nobody maintains. Adding a value requires a row that needs it.
stateVocabulary.live: The slot's own directories hold a real source tree: non-empty, with git history. There is a product here now.
stateVocabulary.shell-claimed: The directory pair exists and BOTH halves are empty - 0 files, no .git, no remote, no history - but a real product exists elsewhere in the tree for which this slot is the declared destination. An empty pre-created shell with something to put in it.
stateVocabulary.shell-empty: The directory pair exists and both halves are empty, and NO product exists anywhere that belongs here. Nothing to copy, nothing to build, nothing to ship. This is the 'no product behind it at all' case, and it is the majority of the matrix.
stateVocabulary.derivedFrom: state is recomputable: non-empty dirs => live; empty dirs and backing != null => shell-claimed; empty dirs and backing == null => shell-empty. It is stored anyway because it is the field a reader actually wants. assert-store-matrix.mjs recomputes it from the disk and from `backing` and fails on disagreement - that check is the only reason storing it is not simply a second copy of a fact.

backing.rule: A slot is BACKED when a real source tree exists TODAY that this slot's product would be built from - either sitting in the slot (filed: true) or sitting elsewhere under Projects/ with this slot as its declared destination (filed: false). Counting capability instead of existence is exactly how fourteen empty directories start reading as a portfolio.

openDecisions.status: STILL OPEN, and 2026-08-19 MOVED IT WITHOUT ANSWERING IT. The pair was filed into Chrome_Web_Store/Chrome/Extensions, which is now `live` and bound to both existing repos. Edge and Firefox are unchanged: `shell-claimed`, empty, boundRemote null, still backed by the same product. So the question is no longer 'where does the pair live' - it is 'do Edge and Firefox get COPIES of the Chrome slot, or repos of their own', and nothing on disk decides it. It now blocks two rows rather than three, which is a smaller blast radius and the same open question. 2026-08-19 SECOND READING - AND THE REPOS EXISTING DOES NOT ANSWER IT EITHER. Nikatru_Edge_Extensions_{Public,Private} and Nikatru_Firefox_Extensions_{Public,Private} now all exist in the org, holding a README and nothing else. Both slots are therefore recorded existsOnGitHub: true and left `shell-claimed`, with boundRemote null: stateVocabulary defines `live` by the SLOT'S OWN DIRECTORIES holding a real source tree, and both halves of both are still 0 files on disk. So the question is now sharper rather than closer to settled - repos of their own EXIST, which is one of the two answers, made available but not chosen, and choosing it means a copy landing in Firefox_AMO and the permanent gecko.id existing in two trees.

openDecisions.question: Does `state: "live"` mean 'carries a copy of the origin', or just 'there is a real tree here'?
openDecisions.status: ANSWERED 2026-08-19, IN THE SAME PULL REQUEST THAT RAISED IT, and the question stands as asked. `live` KEEPS the meaning stateVocabulary gives it - 'the slot's own directories hold a real source tree' - because that is the meaning the disk derives and narrowing it would make the field disagree with the thing it is computed from. What changed is the GUARD: assert-copy-parity.mjs no longer reads `state` as the copy set. It takes the `live` rows whose `backing.product` equals the ORIGIN row's `backing.product`, minus the origin - the first of the three ways out named when this was filed, and the one that entry already called right. Re-measured after the change: exit 3 NOT PROVEN, 0 copies, with Chrome_Web_Store/Chrome/Extensions printed as EXCLUDED by name beside the product that owns it (`fullshot`). It no longer refuses, and it no longer reports a Chrome extension as a missing Flutter copy. THE ROW-LEVEL FIELD IS THE CHEAP END OF backing.products[].claimsSlots: this guard already FAILS when a claim names no row or a backed row is claimed by nobody, so copy-parity reads the same declaration without re-implementing the join. WHAT THE FIX DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: nothing is dropped in silence. A `live` slot of another product is PRINTED with its product; a `live` slot naming NO product is a REFUSAL (exit 2), not an exclusion, because 'unclassifiable' guessed as 'not ours' is the one direction that would let a real, diverged copy of this origin leave the comparison without a word. Four cases in tooling/ci/test/copy-parity.test.mjs hold all of that, including the control that stops the fix from degenerating into 'exclude everything': a live slot carrying the SAME product is still compared and still exits 0.

openDecisions.question: Do the private slots get GitHub remotes at all?
openDecisions.status: OPEN - answering yes re-arms the collision above, and 2026-08-19 MADE ANSWERING IT CARELESSLY MUCH EASIER. The backup repo was renamed INTO this scheme and is now called Nikatru_Android_Apps_Private, the exact name this row derives, so the private half now shows existsOnGitHub: true with a correct-looking name and a wrong-shaped tree behind it. boundRemote is null on purpose. Read collisions[latent-backup-remote-name].escalated20260819 before binding anything.

openDecisions.question: Does the repo name equal the directory name?
openDecisions.status: ANSWERED YES ON 2026-08-19, BY THE OWNER, WHO PERFORMED IT. Every one of the 30 intended repo names exists in the org and equals its directory name, and the five repositories that held the old names were RENAMED rather than replaced, so no history was orphaned. This registry still records the rule as a PROPOSAL in naming.repoNameRule and acted on nothing - see naming.settled20260819. The one item the change left outstanding is not in git and cannot be closed from here: the Cloudflare Pages bindings still name the old repo. See github.renamePins.unobservable[cloudflare-pages].

openDecisions.question: Is tooling/ copied per slot or centralised?
openDecisions.status: OPEN - moves the copy cost by roughly 4x

openDecisions.question: Which slot ships first?
openDecisions.status: OPEN - it should be the store the owner actually intends to submit to next, not the alphabetically first shell

openDecisions.question: Storefront URL shape
openDecisions.status: LOCKED - one product page /apps/<slug> carrying every store link; store COLLECTION pages /<store>/apps; /<store>/apps/<slug> a 301 and /get/<store>/<slug> a 302. Also locked: none of it ships before the Cloudflare repoint. Those collection pages are the first real reader of this file, and they cannot be built before that repoint.
